security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code, placeholders, and diagnostic examples. The Docker Bench command exposes host namespaces and the Docker socket, while the kube-bench command applies a mutable remote manifest. Destructive and high-rate operations also lack consistent approval and authorization controls.

remediation.issue: The Docker Bench example grants host access and mounts the Docker socket.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval, use an isolated audit host, pin the image digest, and document that Docker socket access grants host-equivalent control.

remediation.issue: Destructive infrastructure commands appear without consistent confirmation controls.
remediation.suggestion: Require a reviewed plan, backups, scoped targets, explicit confirmation, and rollback checks before prune, destroy, drain, or cleanup operations.

remediation.issue: The kube-bench example applies a manifest from a mutable remote branch.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a release and commit digest, download the manifest, verify its checksum, review it locally, then apply the reviewed file.

remediation.issue: Load-testing examples omit target authorization and abort conditions.
remediation.suggestion: Require documented ownership, an approved test window, conservative starting rates, monitoring, rate ceilings, and automatic abort thresholds.

content.user_title: Build Reliable DevOps and SRE Workflows
content.value_statement: Complex delivery and reliability work often lacks a consistent operating method. This skill guides CI/CD, Kubernetes, observability, incident response, and infrastructure automation.
actual_capabilities: Designs CI/CD pipelines for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Argo CD, and Tekton.
Produces Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Terraform, OpenTofu, Pulumi, and Ansible configurations.
Defines Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards, logs, traces, alert rules, SLOs, SLIs, and error budgets.
Guides incident triage using USE, RED, DIVE, and structured postmortems.
Plans performance tests, capacity models, chaos experiments, backups, disaster recovery, and cloud cost optimization.
Integrates security scanning and policy tools into delivery workflows.
limitations: Does not provide environment-specific credentials, cluster access, or cloud permissions.
Command examples require validation against the target operating system, tool versions, and organizational controls.
Recommendations depend on accurate architecture, traffic, cost, and incident data supplied by the user.
Does not replace human approval for production changes, privileged access, destructive commands, or load tests.

use_cases.title: Standardize application delivery
use_cases.description: Create reviewed CI/CD, container, Kubernetes, and GitOps plans for repeatable releases across development, staging, and production.

use_cases.title: Investigate production incidents
use_cases.description: Organize evidence, prioritize containment, test likely causes, verify recovery, and produce a structured postmortem.

use_cases.title: Improve reliability investments
use_cases.description: Define SLOs, capacity needs, observability gaps, resilience experiments, and cost actions for an engineering portfolio.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic CI pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my [application] and propose a CI pipeline for [platform]. Include stages, secrets, artifacts, approval gates, validation, and rollback checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs repeatable build and test automation.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Kubernetes deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Kubernetes deployment plan for [service] on [cluster]. Include resources, probes, limits, secrets handling, rollout checks, and rollback steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: An application team is moving a service to Kubernetes.

prompt_templates.title: Define an SLO program
prompt_templates.prompt: Define SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, recording rules, dashboards, and alerts for [service] using [traffic and reliability data]. Explain each threshold.
prompt_templates.scenario: An SRE team needs measurable reliability objectives.

prompt_templates.title: Lead an incident and resilience review
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [incident evidence] for [service]. Prioritize containment, test root-cause hypotheses, define recovery checks, and produce a blameless postmortem with owned actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced team needs incident leadership and long-term prevention.

output_examples.input: Design a delivery workflow for a containerized API deployed to Kubernetes.
output: A staged pipeline plan covering checks, tests, image scanning, promotion, approvals, deployment verification, and rollback.
A configuration inventory listing required workflow, container, Kubernetes, secret, and GitOps artifacts.

output_examples.input: Investigate rising latency and server errors after a production release.
output: An incident sequence that starts with impact confirmation and containment.
Ranked hypotheses linked to metrics, logs, traces, dependencies, resources, and recent changes.
Recovery checks and postmortem actions with owners and deadlines.

output_examples.input: Define reliability objectives for a customer-facing API.
output: Proposed availability and latency indicators based on valid requests and user outcomes.
Error-budget thresholds, burn-rate alerts, dashboard needs, and release decisions.

best_practices: Confirm environment, ownership, permissions, expected impact, maintenance window, and recovery options before operational work.
Review generated plans and configuration changes through version control, automated checks, and human approval.
Start load and resilience tests at low scope, monitor continuously, and stop automatically when safety thresholds fail.
anti_patterns: Run copied commands directly in production without validating placeholders, versions, permissions, and effects.
Apply infrastructure changes or remote manifests without review, pinning, backups, and rollback preparation.
Use production as the first environment for load, chaos, recovery, or migration testing.

faq.question: Can this skill deploy directly to my infrastructure?
faq.answer: It can guide and execute permitted workflows, but access depends on available tools, credentials, and explicit authorization.

faq.question: Which delivery platforms does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Argo CD, Flux, and Tekton patterns.

faq.question: Can it help during a production incident?
faq.answer: Yes. It structures triage, containment, diagnosis, recovery verification, communication, and postmortem actions.

faq.question: Does it support Kubernetes and infrastructure as code?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Terraform, OpenTofu, Pulumi, Ansible, and related operating practices.

faq.question: Will it run destructive commands automatically?
faq.answer: Production, privileged, and destructive actions require review, scoped authorization, backups, and explicit confirmation.

faq.question: Can it define SLOs and observability?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose indicators, objectives, error budgets, metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, and actionable alerts.
